facts: The paper discusses language model adaptation methods.
The language model adaptation setting involves a word list and a raw corpus.
The general method is to segment the raw corpus automatically using a word list.
The general method includes correcting the output sentences by hand.
The general method includes building a model from the segmented corpus.
In the sentence-by-sentence error correction method, the annotator encounters grammatically complicated positions.
Encountering grammatically complicated positions results in a decrease of productivity in the sentence-by-sentence error correction method.
The authors propose to concentrate on correcting the positions in which the words in the list appear by taking a word as a correction unit.
The proposed approach concentrates on correcting the positions in which the words in the list appear.
The proposed approach takes a word as a correction unit.
The proposed approach allows going directly to capturing the statistical behavior of specific words in the application.
The experiments used a variety of methods for preparing a segmented corpus.
The experiments compared the language models by their speech recognition accuracies.
The results showed the advantages of the proposed method.
An annotator is involved in the sentence-by-sentence error correction method.
